Subject: Packaging questions — segmented tiers + vendor add-ons

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran this past our platform team and procurement and have two short packaging questions before we can move to the commercial review:

1) We have two distinct product teams (Clinical Ops & Patient Engagement) that need different throughput profiles. Could we split the account into two concurrent tiers (one higher-throughput, one standard) under a single contract but billed separately? How does seat pooling or overage work in that configuration?

2) We rely on three third-party connectors (telemetry vendor, EHR sync, analytics vendor). Procurement wants those listed as add-ons (monthly flat fee per connector) rather than built into the base seat price. Do you have standard add-on SKUs and proration rules for connector changes mid-cycle?

Attached the draft SOW procurement shared — they asked us to confirm proration and credit terms so legal can prepare an amendment.

Appreciate a concise breakdown; we’re trying to finalize numbers by Friday.

Hi Sara — thanks, and great questions. Long answer short: yes to both, with a few guardrails. Summary below so procurement can include in the amendment.

1) Segmented tiers under one contract
- We can support two independent tiers (Tier A — high-throughput; Tier B — standard) tied to separate seat pools. Billing is per-pool, so each pool gets its own committed-seat pricing and overage rules.
- Seat pooling: optional. If you enable pooling, unused capacity from one pool can offset spikes in the other for a configurable percentage (we typically recommend a 10–20% shared buffer). Pooling changes require a 30-day notice and are pro-rated from the next billing cycle.
- Overage: charged at 1.5x the committed seat rate for that pool, calculated hourly and billed monthly.

2) Vendor connector add-ons & proration
- We offer a connector SKU (CONN-STD) priced at $200/connector/month for standard connectors; enterprise connectors (EHR sync) are $600/month.
- Add/remove mid-cycle: connectors added mid-billing-period are pro-rated daily from the activation date; removals are pro-rated and credited to the next invoice.
- If add-ons increase total committed spend above your next pricing tier, we can lock in a temporary uplift for the remainder of the billing period and re-evaluate at renewal.

Commercial concession options (quick proposal)
- Pilot: 3-month pilot for Clinical Ops on Tier A at a 20% pilot discount for the first 3 months (no commitment) so they can validate throughput.
- Committed discount: 12-month commit across both pools => incremental 10% contract-level discount.
- Waive onboarding fee ($5k) if you sign within 30 days.

I’ve attached an updated pricing spreadsheet with these scenarios so you can run the numbers. If you want, we can draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and signoffs.

Next steps: I can loop in Kimberly (sales lead) and Priyom (pricing) to confirm the formal concession and legal language — want me to send the internal note now or wait for procurement to pick one of the three options?

- Rachel
